chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Beware when one of you wants to ask his Lord for anything from the needs of the world and the Hereafter, that he does not do so until he begins with praising Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and eulogizing Him, and sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then he should ask Allah for his needs.'

key_terms.الثَّنَاءِ: Praising Allah with His beautiful names and attributes
key_terms.حَوَائِجِ الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ: Needs of the world and the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette before making a supplication to God?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the canonical structure of supplication, emphasizing that initiating with divine praise and prophetic blessings (salawat) is a prerequisite for the acceptance of one's needs. In Shia scholarly tradition, this sequence reflects the spiritual protocol of acknowledging Allah's majesty and the Prophet's intercessory status before making personal petitions, ensuring the dua is framed within reverence and gratitude.
